spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the Hawaiian Islands from northwest to southeast over dark ocean with scattered white cumulus and a broad band of white clouds to the south and over the southeastern large island.

plumes.label: pale blue-gray veil southeast of the large island
plumes.visual_description: translucent pale blue-gray veil extending southward off the southeast coast of the large island, distinct from the bright white cumulus over the island

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

evidence: Kilauea was officially erupting (Episode 54 of Halemaumau eruption, WATCH/ORANGE) while Mauna Loa was NORMAL/GREEN not erupting. [E2]
FIRMS shows intense volcanic thermal at Kilauea summit (224 volcanic_thermal pixels) with cluster 4 km from summit and no separate wildfire, consistent with volcanic source. [E3]
Geometry trails from Kilauea: centroid 28.4 km from Kilauea vs 49.6 km from Mauna Loa, and tracked inferred source end 14.2 km from Kilauea vs 38.5 km from Mauna Loa. [E4, E5]
Mask is 92% over ocean (land_frac 0.08) southeast of Hawaii, reliable with no island swallowed; translucent pale blue-gray veil distinct from bright white cumulus supports vog over cloud. [E6, E4]

Measured 3-h drift toward 178 deg south at 5.4 km/h (fit R2 0.7) disagrees with 10-m wind from 81 deg blowing toward ~261 deg west by ~83 deg, exceeding 45 deg tolerance and lowering confidence. [E1, E5]

evidence_cited.text: Kilauea was officially erupting (Episode 54 of Halemaumau eruption, WATCH/ORANGE) while Mauna Loa was NORMAL/GREEN not erupting.
FIRMS shows intense volcanic thermal at Kilauea summit (224 volcanic_thermal pixels) with cluster 4 km from summit and no separate wildfire, consistent with volcanic source.
Geometry trails from Kilauea: centroid 28.4 km from Kilauea vs 49.6 km from Mauna Loa, and tracked inferred source end 14.2 km from Kilauea vs 38.5 km from Mauna Loa.
Mask is 92% over ocean (land_frac 0.08) southeast of Hawaii, reliable with no island swallowed; translucent pale blue-gray veil distinct from bright white cumulus supports vog over cloud.
Measured 3-h drift toward 178 deg south at 5.4 km/h (fit R2 0.7) disagrees with 10-m wind from 81 deg blowing toward ~261 deg west by ~83 deg, exceeding 45 deg tolerance and lowering confidence.

classify.caveats: 10-m ERA5 wind blows toward ~261 deg (W) while 3-h tracked drift is toward 178 deg (S), ~83 deg mismatch that lowers confidence; faint veil adjacent to extensive southern cloud band so cloud contamination cannot be fully excluded; single wind point may not represent plume-layer flow around island terrain.

kilauea.activity_summary: Episode 54 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption continues as of 12:15 p.m. HST on August 25.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
